title: Studying line defect at Deconfined Quantum Criticality via fuzzy sphere regularization
authors: Shutao Liu, Shuai Yang, Jie Lou, Yan Chen
abstract: The interplay between bulk critical fluctuations and nontrivial topology can enrich defect physics and give rise to novel defect universality classes. Understanding the fate of such defects therefore constitutes an important open problem. In this work, we studied a particularly simple setting: a (0+1)-dimensional pinning-field defect coupled to a (2+1)-dimensional deconfined quantum critical bulk. Using the fuzzy-sphere regularization, we numerically investigated the defect operator spectrum and extracted several universal quantities characterizing the defect conformal fixed point, including the scaling dimensions of defect-changing(creating) operators and the defect \(g\)-function. These results establish the first numerical characterization of line-defect conformal data at deconfined quantum criticality and may stimulate further investigations of defect critical phenomena in topological quantum critical matter.
summary: This paper theoretically investigates line defects embedded in a Deconfined Quantum Critical Point (DQCP) bulk using fuzzy-sphere regularization. By analyzing the defect operator spectrum across the renormalization group flow, the authors characterize the universal properties of the defect's conformal fixed point. The results confirm the existence of a stable defect critical phase, demonstrating the robustness of this physics across different underlying symmetries (SO(5) and O(4)).
main_problem: The study investigates the universal properties of one-dimensional line defects embedded within a two-dimensional Deconfined Quantum Critical Point (DQCP) bulk.
main_result: The numerical analysis establishes the first characterization of line-defect conformal data at DQCP, suggesting the existence of a stable, non-trivial defect conformal fixed point.
method: The authors employed fuzzy-sphere regularization and numerical exact diagonalization to analyze the Renormalization Group (RG) flow of the defect operator spectrum.
model_or_system: The system models a (0+1)-dimensional pinning-field defect coupled to a (2+1)-dimensional DQCP bulk, which is related to an SO(5) symmetry. The analysis is extended to an O(4) symmetry case to test universality.
key_observables: Defect operator spectrum, defect g-function, scaling dimensions of defect-changing/creating operators, and correlation functions.
important_parameters: The defect coupling strength ($h_d$), which is varied from 0 (bulk fixed point) to $\infty$ (defect fixed point).
main_assumptions: The analysis relies on the fuzzy-sphere regularization framework, and the DQCP realizations are assumed to be weakly first-order.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the evolution of excitation states along the RG flow, show finite-size extrapolation of scaling dimensions, and display the resulting defect conformal multiplets.
paper_structure: The paper systematically analyzes the RG flow from the bulk fixed point to the defect fixed point for the SO(5) DQCP, extracts universal conformal data, and then confirms the robustness of these findings by repeating the analysis for an O(4) symmetric DQCP.
why_interesting: The study provides a rigorous theoretical framework for understanding how topological defects modify critical behavior in strongly correlated quantum matter, which is relevant to understanding boundary effects in quantum materials.
